label: <DEL> in short sequences starting with w/z/t/0/2, plus early f/x inputs
explanation: Two loosely related components. (1) The delimiter step (about 40% of activation mass, and every top activation): strongest when the sequence is short (L=3-5) and the first original token is w, z, t, 0 or 2. (2) Original-phase inputs f or x at early positions (t=1-4), about 39% of mass. It never fires at t=0 and is weak in the copy phase (11% of mass, with scattered activations). Precision is low (about 0.23): most DEL steps and most early f/x steps stay below threshold, so the neuron seems to respond to a graded mix of the input token and the history (seen w/z/t/0/2) that a boolean predicate cannot capture. Dev F1 is about 0.30 and mass recall 0.56.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: f, x, h, 3; t=2: f, x, 3, h; t=3: f, x, 1, 3) and the first original token (most: w, z, 0, t, 2, i; least: a, x, y, v); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, L=4 & t=3, t=2.
